item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Pensacola resident is sharing his story of overcoming addiction after an accident and series of poor decisions led him down a difficult path, according to reporting from WKRG-TV 5. The man credits Bright Bridge Ministries with helping him turn his life around. His account highlights how a single traumatic event can cascade into substance abuse,…
item.content:encoded:
A Pensacola resident is sharing his story of overcoming addiction after an accident and series of poor decisions led him down a difficult path, according to reporting from WKRG-TV 5.

The man credits Bright Bridge Ministries with helping him turn his life around. His account highlights how a single traumatic event can cascade into substance abuse, but also underscores the role local recovery programs play in helping people regain stability.

Bright Bridge Ministries, which operates recovery and support services in the Pensacola area, has become a resource for residents battling addiction. The organization focuses on faith-based recovery and community reintegration.

The story is part of WKRG's ongoing "Drexel on the Road" series, which profiles individuals and organizations making an impact across the Gulf Coast region.

item.title: Bay Minette Elementary Celebrates Young Cancer Survivors During Awareness Month
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Bay Minette Elementary School in Baldwin County is joining a nationwide push to raise awareness about childhood cancer, with school leaders honoring students who've faced the disease. The celebration is part of a broader effort by Baldwin County Public Schools to "go gold" — the official color of Childhood Cancer Awareness Month — in recognition…
item.content:encoded:
Bay Minette Elementary School in Baldwin County is joining a nationwide push to raise awareness about childhood cancer, with school leaders honoring students who've faced the disease. The celebration is part of a broader effort by Baldwin County Public Schools to "go gold" — the official color of Childhood Cancer Awareness Month — in recognition of young people battling or recovering from cancer.

The event gives the school community a chance to recognize the resilience of students who've dealt with a serious health challenge while continuing their education. Childhood cancer survivors often show remarkable strength, and schools across the region are using September as an opportunity to amplify awareness and support for affected families.

Baldwin County schools have embraced the awareness campaign, with multiple campuses displaying gold in various forms throughout the month. The recognition serves both as encouragement for the honored students and as a reminder to the broader school community about the importance of health awareness and support systems for children facing medical hardships.

item.title: DeSantis Appoints Three to Apalachicola Water and Sewer District
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced today the appointment of three new members to the Apalachicola Water and Sewer District board: Jimmy Gander, Torben Madson III, and Mark Milliken. Gander is owner and vice president of JV Gander Oil Company and a former Franklin County School Board member. He's a Florida National Guard veteran who holds a bachelor's…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced today the appointment of three new members to the Apalachicola Water and Sewer District board: Jimmy Gander, Torben Madson III, and Mark Milliken.

Gander is owner and vice president of JV Gander Oil Company and a former Franklin County School Board member. He's a Florida National Guard veteran who holds a bachelor's degree from the University of West Florida. Madson III owns and manages The PEO Law Firm and serves on the Franklin County Parks and Recreation Board. He earned his law degree from the University of Miami and undergraduate degree from the University of Florida. Milliken, president of Gulf Unmanned Systems Center, is a retired Navy Rear Admiral with experience as a senior manager at Wyle, Inc. and vice president of maritime solutions for Elbit Systems of America. He graduated from the U.S. Naval Academy with a degree in analytical management.

The appointments come as the Apalachicola area continues to manage water resource challenges in the region.

item.title: DeSantis Appoints Two to Applied Behavior Analysis Task Force
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced Friday the appointment of Kale Baker and David Brown to the Applied Behavior Analysis Task Force, according to a release from the Governor's Press Office. Baker, who holds a master's degree in social work from Barry University, currently serves as Vice President at Molina Healthcare. He previously worked as Director…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced Friday the appointment of Kale Baker and David Brown to the Applied Behavior Analysis Task Force, according to a release from the Governor's Press Office.

Baker, who holds a master's degree in social work from Barry University, currently serves as Vice President at Molina Healthcare. He previously worked as Director of Regulatory Affairs at Molina Healthcare and held several positions at Magellan Complete Care and Magellan Financial Group, including Senior Director of Account Management and Director of Care Coordination.

Brown, a graduate of New England College and Florida Gulf Coast University with degrees in criminal justice and social work respectively, is President and Co-Founder of Family Initiative. He has also served as Program Coordinator for the Quality Parenting Initiative and Director of Programs for the Children's Network of Southwest Florida.

item.title: DeSantis Names Education Official to Independent Education Commission
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis has appointed Kevin O'Farrell, currently the Executive Vice President of Workforce and Strategic Initiatives at Polk State College, to the Commission for Independent Education, according to an announcement from the Governor's Press Office on Friday. O'Farrell brings extensive experience in Florida's education and workforce…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis has appointed Kevin O'Farrell, currently the Executive Vice President of Workforce and Strategic Initiatives at Polk State College, to the Commission for Independent Education, according to an announcement from the Governor's Press Office on Friday.

O'Farrell brings extensive experience in Florida's education and workforce sectors. Before his current role at Polk State, he served as Senior Chancellor for Higher Education and Workforce Development with the Florida Department of Education. He holds a doctorate in curriculum and instruction from the University of South Florida, along with master's degrees in political science and public administration from the same institution.

The appointment is subject to confirmation by the Florida Senate. The Commission for Independent Education oversees Florida's private schools and education programs that operate outside the traditional public school system.

item.title: DeSantis Reappoints Leon Medical Centers CEO to Fish and Wildlife Commission
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis has announced the reappointment of Albert Maury to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, according to the Governor's Press Office. Maury, who serves as President and Chief Executive Officer of Leon Medical Centers, LLC, will continue his role on the state commission pending Florida Senate confirmation. Maury…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis has announced the reappointment of Albert Maury to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, according to the Governor's Press Office. Maury, who serves as President and Chief Executive Officer of Leon Medical Centers, LLC, will continue his role on the state commission pending Florida Senate confirmation.

Maury brings business and nonprofit leadership experience to the position. He previously served on the Florida International University Board of Trustees and holds a bachelor's degree in finance and accounting from FIU. The reappointment was announced Friday.

The Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission oversees management of Florida's fish and wildlife resources, hunting and fishing regulations, and conservation efforts across the state. Commission members are appointed by the governor and require Senate confirmation.

item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced Friday the appointment of Brian McBroom to serve as Walton County Tax Collector, according to the Governor's Press Office.

McBroom currently serves as Chief Tax Collector for the Walton County Tax Collector's Office. He holds a 2023 Distinguished Service Award from the Florida Tax Collector's Association and earned his associate degree from Northwest Florida State College.

Beyond his tax collector duties, McBroom is active in the Panhandle community as president of the Freeport & South Walton Kiwanis Club. The appointment takes effect immediately.

item.title: Puerto Rico Dem Chair Campaigns in Orlando This Weekend
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The chairman of the Democratic Party of Puerto Rico will be in the Orlando area Saturday and Sunday campaigning alongside Florida Democratic candidates and officials, according to a media advisory from the Florida Democratic Party. Luis Dávila Pernas, who also serves as a political analyst for Telemundo Puerto Rico and sits on the Democratic…
item.content:encoded:
The chairman of the Democratic Party of Puerto Rico will be in the Orlando area Saturday and Sunday campaigning alongside Florida Democratic candidates and officials, according to a media advisory from the Florida Democratic Party.

Luis Dávila Pernas, who also serves as a political analyst for Telemundo Puerto Rico and sits on the Democratic National Committee's Rules and Bylaws Committee, will participate in canvassing efforts and hold interviews in both English and Spanish. His visit comes as Democrats seek to mobilize Puerto Rican voters in Florida ahead of November's elections.

Dávila Pernas will appear with U.S. Rep. Darren Soto, former Miami Mayor David Jolly, Annette Taddeo (who is running for Chief Financial Officer), and Samuel Vilchez Santiago (a candidate for House District 43). Saturday's events include a 10-11 a.m. canvass in Kissimmee followed by an afternoon open to media interviews. On Sunday morning, he'll attend a canvass kickoff at Tainos Bakery in Orlando.

The visit underscores Democratic efforts to engage Puerto Rican communities in Florida, which represent a significant voting bloc in the state. Organizers say Dávila Pernas will discuss the issues driving Puerto Rican voters and how federal policy affects families both in Florida and on the island.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County officials are opening the door for community feedback on a stormwater management study focused on the Bayou Marcus Basin, according to WKRG News 5.

The county is actively soliciting public input as part of the study process, which examines stormwater challenges and potential solutions in the basin area. Officials have not yet released specific details about the study's timeline, scope, or planned improvements, but the call for public comment suggests the project is in an early consultation phase.

Residents and business owners interested in weighing in on the stormwater study are encouraged to participate through the county's formal input process. Those wanting to learn more or submit comments should contact Escambia County officials directly for meeting dates, submission deadlines, and additional study information.

Gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds will visit Florida A&M University on Tuesday, September 29, to discuss his vision for the state during a student town hall event. The appearance at FAMU's Lee Hall in Tallahassee begins at 7 p.m., with doors opening at 6:15 p.m.

The event gives FAMU students a chance to ask questions and hear directly from Donalds about his platform and priorities for Florida's future. Media outlets are invited to cover the town hall but must RSVP in advance by emailing jenn@sachsmedia.com. A media check-in table will be set up at the event.

The town hall is not open to the general public and is restricted to FAMU students and credentialed media members.

The conviction marks another federal prosecution targeting gang-related drug trafficking in the Pensacola area. Federal authorities have intensified enforcement efforts against organized drug distribution networks operating in Northwest Florida.

item.title: George County offers medication disposal during Drug Take Back Day
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Residents in George County, Mississippi, have an opportunity to safely dispose of unused or expired medications during National Drug Take Back Day, according to WKRG News 5. The George County Sheriff's Office is hosting the event, which allows community members to drop off medications they no longer need or have passed their expiration dates. The…
item.content:encoded:
Residents in George County, Mississippi, have an opportunity to safely dispose of unused or expired medications during National Drug Take Back Day, according to WKRG News 5. The George County Sheriff's Office is hosting the event, which allows community members to drop off medications they no longer need or have passed their expiration dates.

The program accepts most medications but has a few exceptions. Inhalers and needles cannot be included in the disposal program due to safety concerns. The initiative is part of a broader national effort to prevent prescription drug misuse and reduce environmental contamination from improperly discarded medications.

Families and individuals looking to clean out medicine cabinets can use this resource to responsibly eliminate old prescriptions and over-the-counter drugs. The Sheriff's Office encourages residents to take advantage of the safe disposal option rather than flushing medications or throwing them in the trash, where they can pose risks to water supplies and wildlife.

Pensacola is experiencing pleasant early autumn conditions Friday afternoon, with partly cloudy skies and mild temperatures. According to Florida Gulf Signal, the area showed scattered clouds with clearing trends as of 2 p.m., with air temperatures hovering around 76 degrees and northeast winds at nearly 12 knots.

Tide activity is moving downward through Friday evening, with low tide expected around 6:43 p.m. at roughly 1 foot, followed by a high tide just after midnight at 1.1 feet. The moderate northeast breeze suggests typical fall weather patterns for the Pensacola coast.

Conditions remain favorable for outdoor activities through the remainder of the afternoon and into the evening.

item.title: Sinatra Tribute Concert Comes to Naval Aviation Museum Oct. 23
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Frank Sinatra's greatest hits will fill the Blue Angels Atrium at the National Naval Aviation Museum on October 23, when bandleader Brian Duprey and a 13-piece orchestra perform "A Symphonic Tribute to Frank Sinatra: Come Fly with Me." The evening celebrates the legendary crooner's timeless catalog in one of Pensacola's most distinctive venues,…
item.content:encoded:
Frank Sinatra's greatest hits will fill the Blue Angels Atrium at the National Naval Aviation Museum on October 23, when bandleader Brian Duprey and a 13-piece orchestra perform "A Symphonic Tribute to Frank Sinatra: Come Fly with Me." The evening celebrates the legendary crooner's timeless catalog in one of Pensacola's most distinctive venues, surrounded by historic naval aircraft.

Tickets range from $50 for general seating to $75 for reserved sections. A cocktail hour with a cash bar begins at 5:30 p.m., with the performance starting at 7 p.m. Interested listeners can purchase tickets through the museum's website at navalaviationmuseum.org.

Because the museum sits on Naval Air Station Pensacola, visitors without a Department of Defense ID must complete additional paperwork. Anyone 18 or older without a DoD card needs to submit a SECNAV Form 5512 by October 9 to Riley Stephens at rstephens@navalaviationmuseum.org. Non-DoD visitors must buy tickets by October 9 as well to allow time for base security processing. Those with questions can contact Stephens directly.

item.title: Linda McCartney Honored With U.S. Postal Service Stamp Series
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Postal Service is introducing a new stamp series celebrating photographer, musician and animal rights advocate Linda McCartney, according to an announcement today from the agency. The stamps, now available at post offices nationwide including those across Northern Florida, feature McCartney's still life and landscape photography.…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Postal Service is introducing a new stamp series celebrating photographer, musician and animal rights advocate Linda McCartney, according to an announcement today from the agency. The stamps, now available at post offices nationwide including those across Northern Florida, feature McCartney's still life and landscape photography.

McCartney, who lived from 1941 to 1998, had a wide-ranging career that made her a cultural icon. She was the first female photographer to have her work featured on the cover of Rolling Stone magazine in 1968, and later became the first person to both photograph a cover and appear on one when she and husband Paul McCartney graced the magazine in 1974. Beyond photography, she was a founding member of the band Wings, a published author of multiple photography collections and cookbooks, and a pioneering advocate for vegetarianism and animal rights.

Postmaster General David Steiner remarked that McCartney's legacy embodied the values the stamp program seeks to recognize. "Linda McCartney's life and work represents the best of what the USPS stamp program seeks to recognize: art that endures, art that enriches, art that uplifts people and art that is universal," Steiner said during a dedication ceremony at The Museum of Modern Art in New York.

McCartney's daughter Mary McCartney also attended the ceremony, describing her mother as someone who was "a pioneer" and "definitely ahead of her time." McCartney's photography collections have been exhibited at prestigious institutions including the Victoria and Albert Museum in London and the Royal Photographic Society in Bath, England.

item.content:encoded: Foley Police Department is searching for a man following a serious dog attack that left a woman injured, according to a department news release. Officers responded to the 13000 block of McGaster Trail on Thursday after the incident. The woman sustained significant injuries in the attack, though specific details about her condition were not immediately disclosed.
